source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue every droplet precaution indefinitely because pathogen-specific stopping criteria do not exist","B":"Stop every droplet precaution exactly 24 hours after it begins regardless of diagnosis or symptoms","C":"Use organism- and condition-specific criteria while the transmission risk persists, following current guidance","D":"Discontinue precautions whenever the client requests it, independent of transmission risk or guidance"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC states that Transmission-Based Precautions remain in effect while transmission risk persists, with duration depending on the pathogen, clinical course, testing, treatment, and applicable facility or public-health guidance.
source_row.source_detail: Type and Duration of Precautions Recommended for Selected Infections and Conditions; updated Feb. 7, 2025; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Isolation Precautions, Appendix A and Transmission-Based Precautions
source_row.stem: A client is on droplet precautions for a respiratory infection. How is the duration of transmission-based precautions determined?
